text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Philips Electronics to conduct probe itself into insider trading allegations at its unit Pie Medical. (p1)
- Takeover of computer maker Commodore by rival Tulip falls through. (p1)
- Number of new companies in the 1997 first half down to 7,700 from 9,400 in same period last year. (p1).
- Temp agency Randstad eyes financially troubled Amsterdam port labour pool. (p1)
- Fokker Space looks back at a disappointing 1996. (3) DE VOLKSKRANT
- Banks and financial institutions issue report on dubious transactions last year. (p2)
- European Commission forces the Netherlands to allow imports of cornflakes with added iron and vitamins. (p2) DE TELEGRAAF
- Economic affairs minister Hans Wijers in the race to become chief of Dutch PTT KPN next year. (p1)
- Junior finance minister Wim Vermeend's tax rules make buying a business too complex, says federation of tax advisors. (p19)
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM and U.S. partner NorthWest agree on parametres of their accord. (p21) TROUW
- KLM and its pilots bury the hadget. (p7) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- 20 eastern Europe specialists at Fortis' merchant bank MeesPierson leave for ABN AMRO . (p10)
